about: Caleb Williams Injury shows the Chicago Bears quarterback sitting on a sideline cart in pouring rain, a towel over his legs, one arm thrust straight up in a thumbs up. His face doesn't match the gesture: he looks flat, tired and a little stunned while fans in yellow ponchos watch from the stands behind him. The joke is that mismatch. The thumbs up says "I'm good" while everything else in the picture says the day has gone badly, which makes it perfect for anyone insisting they are fine right after something went wrong.
origin: The photo shows Williams, wearing his number 18 Bears jersey, being taken off the field during a rainy game at Soldier Field. It spread as a reaction image and imgflip template under the name Caleb Williams Injury.
usage:
The top box sets up the bad situation in first person: what just happened to you. The bottom box is the brave-face reply, usually some version of "I'm fine", "all good" or "still coming to work tomorrow".

The thumbs up is the punchline, so the setup should be clearly painful: a failed exam, a crashed deploy, a breakup, a sprained ankle, a fantasy team in last place. Keep the tone self-deprecating; it reads best as you laughing at your own disaster.
